text: QCP Market Colour, 3 August 2026 The US has joined Japan in a rare coordinated effort to support the yen, with the New York Fed purchasing yen on behalf of the US Treasury during Friday's operation. It was the first coordinated US–Japan FX intervention since 2011 and the first joint operation specifically supporting the yen since 1998. The timing puts the long end of the Treasury curve firmly in focus. The 30-year yield reached approximately 5.27% on Friday, its highest since 2007, while the 10-year breakeven inflation rate remained near 2.28%. That has kept attention on the role of issuance, investor demand and cross-border flows alongside inflation expectations. For crypto, a rapid yen appreciation can contribute to the unwinding of yen-funded positions and spill over into broader risk assets. However, a more stable currency could also reduce the need for repeated intervention and remove one potential source of pressure on Treasury-market liquidity. The episode is not a clear directional signal for digital assets. Instead, it shows why USD/JPY, Japanese funding conditions and long-dated Treasury yields are increasingly relevant to the liquidity environment surrounding BTC and ETH. Is Treasury action becoming as important as Fed communication in shaping global financial conditions? Read the full QCP Market Colour here.

text: There's this stigma that you're doing it wrong by spending your early 20's grinding for money. Not in the sense that money is bad and you shouldn't be doing it, but sacrificing majority or all of your social experiences/quality of life to purse it. As someone's who's 25 now and spent ages 19-24 more focused on self improvement and perfection in my crafts than 99.99% of society, I can whole heartedly say it was worth it. The biggest reason might not be why you would think though. Yes I've had a lot of success and live life by my own terms, although the biggest reason is that the older I get, the more I feel my raw horsepower for work output slipping. Back when I was 22 and still trying to reach a place where I felt like a "professional" in my work/finding large success, my engine was never ending and I could will discipline with the click of my fingers. 14 hour work days didn't even get a second thought and was second nature to breathing. There may be a variable in that relates to the excess partying I've done over the past 12 months, however I do tend to notice that my engine and discipline to immediately tap into focused deep work isn't quite the same as it was a few years ago. Scienticifically this shouldn't really be true. What I would attribute it to is the early stage curiosity of incremental progress with every trade, business or self improvement piece you level up on. Climb to the peak of the mountain and the second, third, forth time round no longer feels as exciting and generates that same dopamine. Early on I had a motto that if I didn't have 8 figs by 25 I'd kill myself lol. Everything in my early years was about proving to myself that I had the capabilities to compete with the best in the world inside this weird bubble on the internet. When everything was uncertain, brute force effort felt rewarding. When you've already achieved competence, your brain becomes much more selective about where it wants to spend effort. So my decline in "horsepower" seems to be more ascribed to looking for selective high leverage problems. Other than trying to build a perfect read with onchain, the 14 hour days don't feel as beneficial since a lot of the edge/uncertainty has been removed with AI's development. It really does feel like we've entered the era of "work smarter, not harder". Raw IQ felt a much stronger precursor to success vs tenacity 5 years ago compared to now. Information was harder to get your hands on, ideas and theses couldn't be extrapolated down 10 different rabbit holes with a single prompt. The world didn't operate on 1 min timeframes as information had a hierarchy of digestion it would flow down, from the sharps to the normies. Times have changed where your mid curves have custom built LLM's and agents which significantly close the distribution gap of knowledge. On the contrary, I think we do approach a window in the next 1-2 years where we reach such a high level of certainty with quality of models that the pendulum swings back to uncertainty in some type of way. The job force is under mass reconstruction, geopolitics is reaching its pinnacle in innovation wars, the acceleration curve is about to hit the dot com boom ten fold. Personally I haven't found the past 12-18 months overly exciting as it's felt we're coming to the end of a forecastable 5-8 year chapter. If my hunch is right then we're currently in a 2017-19 innovation cycle, where the next couple years set the tone for the coming decade.

text: Coldcard Suspected of Facing a Fourth Organized Attack Wave, Involving ~388.9 BTC Alex Thorn, Head of Research at Galaxy Research, said a fourth organized attack wave may be targeting Coldcard users. Between blocks 960,778 and 960,792, 218 transactions involving 462 victim addresses and 216 fresh destinations moved ~388.9 BTC. Activity was ~45 times higher than the pre-incident baseline, with some funds already swept to second-hop addresses. Similar transactions remain pending in the mempool, and confirmed transactions signal RBF opt-in. Users should move funds off Coldcard devices immediately and use higher fees; RBF may offer a way out for eligible transactions. Previously, Galaxy Research identified three suspected attack waves targeting Coldcard-generated addresses, affecting 4,585 addresses and draining 1,367.05 BTC worth approximately $88.6 million. Coldcard said it halted shipments and destroyed all remaining COLDCARD devices with the vulnerable firmware. Satscard, Opendime, and Tapsigner are unaffected. The patched firmware protects newly generated seeds, but users must create a new seed and move funds from any seed generated on the vulnerable firmware. — link
